concepts.prompt: Every view shows the complete building from a slightly elevated three-quarter angle: front three-quarter, side, and rear three-quarter views. The Great Sky Aviary as ONE single building, like the reference aviary but without any cliff, bridge or island under it: a wide perfectly round stone drum 56 metres across and 10 metres tall, ringed with 16 tall pointed-arch windows evenly spaced, royal-blue wing banners hanging between the windows, a carved stone cornice on top. From the drum rises a large hemispherical dome of gilded iron and glass to 40 metres total height: thick gold primary ribs running from the drum to the top, a fine grid of gold mullions, and tinted pale-blue glass panels that clearly read as glass, not empty. On the very top of the dome a small round stone-and-gold lantern cupola with arched openings and a gold finial. Four slender round stone belvedere towers 24 metres tall with conical slate-blue roofs and gold finials are fused into the drum wall at the four diagonal corners (two at the front, two at the back). Two large open arched entrances, 6 metres wide and 7.5 metres tall, exactly opposite each other, one in the middle of the front face and one in the middle of the back face, so you can see through the building's open interior floor. The whole thing sits on a flat round stone base. Broad, low, wide silhouette: the drum is much wider than it is tall. Stylised-realism game asset in the Palworld / Animo art style, single isolated object on a plain neutral background, even soft daylight, no landscape, no cliffs, no clouds, no sky, no people. Materials: pale warm-grey weathered limestone ashlar (#a89c8a to #c4b8a4, never pure white) in coursed blocks with soft moss in the joints; slate-blue roof tile (#3d4a66); gilded gold ribs and accents (#c9a24a); royal-blue fabric banners with a white and gold wing emblem; honey-coloured timber only for doors, balconies and planks; warm amber window glass as a distinct saturated colour. Absolutely no red, no oxblood, no maroon, no pink anywhere. No half-timbering, no cream plaster, no thatch. Flat ground contact at the base.
